modules.productionQuestion: The database has 500 max connections but dies at 300. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Each connection consumes memory and workers; the practical limit is lower than max_connections and depends on workload
modules.simMechanic: Database with connection and memory sliders; refusal point
modules.breakCondition: Connections exhaust memory before the configured max

modules.title: Read-After-Write Consistency
modules.purpose: Keep a user's own writes visible
modules.productionQuestion: A user saves a setting and the next page load shows the old value. How do you fix it without going back to the primary for everything?
modules.learningDelta: Read-after-write requires routing the user's reads to a consistent source for a window, or propagating a version token
modules.simMechanic: User session across replicas; policy switch; stale reads
modules.breakCondition: A user sees their own write rolled back

modules.title: Database Failover and DNS
modules.purpose: Understand why clients keep hitting the old writer
modules.productionQuestion: The database failed over but the app still writes to the old primary. What did DNS do?
modules.learningDelta: Managed failover updates a DNS name, but client caches, connection pools, and TTLs determine how fast traffic moves
modules.simMechanic: Writer failure with DNS and pool behavior; reconnect time
modules.breakCondition: Stale DNS or pooled connections keep writing to the old node
modules.sources: AWS RDS failover docs; Aurora failover docs

modules.title: Split Brain: Two Writers, One Truth
modules.purpose: Prevent divergent writes during a partition
modules.productionQuestion: Two database nodes both accept writes during a network partition. How do you recover?
modules.learningDelta: Split brain requires fencing, quorum, or a single-writer design; reconciliation after divergence is expensive and sometimes impossible
modules.simMechanic: Two-node cluster with partition; divergent writes
modules.breakCondition: Both nodes accept writes and data diverges
modules.sources: PostgreSQL HA docs; AWS multi-AZ docs

modules.title: Backups and Point-in-Time Recovery
modules.purpose: Recover to the right second, not just the last backup
modules.productionQuestion: A bad migration deletes rows at 14:07. How do you restore without losing 14:00–14:07?
modules.learningDelta: PITR combines a base backup with continuous logs; recovery point and restore time are different objectives
modules.simMechanic: Backup timeline with delete event; restore point and time
modules.breakCondition: Restore loses data inside the backup interval
modules.sources: AWS RDS backup docs; PostgreSQL PITR docs

modules.title: DR Drills: Prove RTO and RPO
modules.purpose: Test recovery before the real incident
modules.productionQuestion: The DR plan says 15 minutes RTO. Has anyone measured it?
modules.learningDelta: Untested recovery is a hypothesis; drills measure restore time, data loss, DNS cutover, and application readiness
modules.simMechanic: Regional failover drill with timed steps; measured RTO
modules.breakCondition: The drill misses RTO because a dependency was forgotten
modules.sources: AWS disaster recovery whitepaper; Google SRE Workbook

modules.title: Vacuum and Bloat
modules.purpose: Reclaim space without locking the table
modules.productionQuestion: A table grows despite deletes and queries slow down. What is bloat doing?
modules.learningDelta: PostgreSQL MVCC keeps dead tuples until vacuum; bloat increases I/O and can make plans worse, while aggressive vacuum competes for resources
modules.simMechanic: Table with updates/deletes; bloat and query time
modules.breakCondition: Dead tuples accumulate and scans slow down

modules.title: Locks and Deadlocks
modules.purpose: Find the transaction holding the lock
modules.productionQuestion: Writes hang and the database reports deadlocks. Which query do you inspect first?
modules.learningDelta: Lock waits and deadlocks come from transaction ordering; pg_locks and wait events reveal the blocker, but killing it has consequences
modules.simMechanic: Transaction timeline with row locks; deadlock and wait graph
modules.breakCondition: Two transactions deadlock and the app retries blindly

modules.title: Long Transactions: Locks, Bloat, and Lag
modules.purpose: Bound transaction duration before it causes an outage
modules.productionQuestion: A reporting query runs for 40 minutes and replication lag climbs. What is the chain?
modules.learningDelta: Long transactions hold snapshots and locks, delay vacuum, and can block replication; they turn a read into a system-wide problem
modules.simMechanic: Primary with long query; locks, bloat, and replica lag
modules.breakCondition: A long transaction blocks vacuum and drives replica lag
modules.sources: PostgreSQL vacuum docs; AWS RDS best practices

modules.title: Indexing: The Right Index for the Query
modules.purpose: Add an index without making writes worse
modules.productionQuestion: A query is slow and adding an index doubles write latency. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: Indexes trade read speed for write cost and space; the query plan, selectivity, and column order decide whether an index helps
modules.simMechanic: Query with index builder; read and write latency
modules.breakCondition: An index is unused because the predicate is not sargable
modules.interviewAngle: Choose an index; read a plan
modules.sources: PostgreSQL index docs; Use the Index Luke

modules.title: Query Plans: Why the Index Is Ignored
modules.purpose: Read a plan before changing a query
modules.productionQuestion: An index exists but the planner chooses a sequential scan. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Plans depend on statistics, selectivity, cost, and predicates; stale stats or functions on columns defeat indexes
modules.simMechanic: Planner with row counts and stats; plan choice
modules.breakCondition: A stale statistic causes a nested loop over millions of rows

modules.title: N+1 Queries: Count the Round Trips
modules.purpose: Find the query pattern that multiplies latency
modules.productionQuestion: A page loads 200 items and makes 201 queries. Where do you fix it?
modules.learningDelta: N+1 comes from per-item queries; batching, joins, or dataloaders reduce round trips and connection pressure
modules.simMechanic: Page rendering with query counter; item count slider
modules.breakCondition: Query count scales with page size and p99 explodes
modules.sources: PostgreSQL join docs; application ORM docs

modules.title: Partitioning and Sharding
modules.purpose: Split data without breaking queries
modules.productionQuestion: A table is too large for one writer. Do you partition, shard, or archive?
modules.learningDelta: Partitioning splits one logical table for maintenance; sharding splits writers across nodes and adds routing and cross-shard complexity
modules.simMechanic: Table growth with strategy switch; query latency and hotspots
modules.breakCondition: A cross-shard query or hot partition dominates latency
modules.sources: PostgreSQL partitioning docs; AWS sharding guidance

modules.title: Hot Partitions
modules.purpose: Find the partition taking most of the traffic
modules.productionQuestion: One tenant's partition receives 60% of writes and its disk is full. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: A hot partition is a data-distribution problem; splitting the key or isolating the tenant changes the balance and the operational model
modules.simMechanic: Partitioned table with tenant traffic; per-partition load
modules.breakCondition: One partition saturates while others are idle
modules.sources: AWS DynamoDB partition guidance; PostgreSQL docs

modules.title: Multi-AZ vs Multi-Region
modules.purpose: Choose a failure domain and be honest about RTO
modules.productionQuestion: The business needs 99.99% and 15-minute RTO. Is Multi-AZ enough?
modules.learningDelta: Multi-AZ protects against an AZ failure with a synchronous standby; multi-region protects against a region failure with asynchronous lag and higher RTO
modules.simMechanic: Failure toggle by AZ and region; availability and data loss
modules.breakCondition: A region failure exceeds the RTO with only Multi-AZ
modules.sources: AWS RDS Multi-AZ docs; AWS disaster recovery

modules.title: Cross-AZ Latency and Cost
modules.purpose: Keep chatty database traffic inside a zone
modules.productionQuestion: The database bill includes a large cross-AZ transfer line. Why is the app talking across zones?
modules.learningDelta: Cross-AZ traffic adds latency and cost; reader placement, chatty queries, and retry loops multiply it
modules.simMechanic: Multi-AZ database and app; traffic paths and cost
modules.breakCondition: Cross-AZ transfer grows faster than request volume
modules.sources: AWS data transfer pricing; Aurora docs

modules.title: Aurora Serverless Scaling
modules.purpose: Understand cold starts and capacity units
modules.productionQuestion: A serverless database is slow after idle periods. What is happening?
modules.learningDelta: Aurora Serverless scales capacity in units and may need to resume; pooling, min capacity, and warm traffic change the experience
modules.simMechanic: Serverless DB with idle periods; latency and ACU
modules.breakCondition: A cold resume breaches the request timeout

modules.title: Parameter Groups: Change With a Plan
modules.purpose: Apply database settings without a surprise restart
modules.productionQuestion: A parameter change improves one query and breaks another. How do you roll it out?
modules.learningDelta: Parameter groups apply engine settings; some are dynamic, some require reboot, and cluster-level settings have different scope
modules.simMechanic: Parameter change with apply mode; performance and restart
modules.breakCondition: A static parameter requires a reboot during peak traffic

modules.title: Storage Autoscaling
modules.purpose: Avoid a full disk without unbounded growth
modules.productionQuestion: Disk usage climbs and autoscaling has a maximum. What happens at the cap?
modules.learningDelta: Storage autoscaling adds capacity within a maximum; growth rate, retention, and temporary files determine whether it saves you
modules.simMechanic: Disk usage with autoscaling cap; full-disk failure
modules.breakCondition: Storage hits the autoscaling maximum and writes fail

modules.title: Replication Thread Bottlenecks
modules.purpose: Find why a replica cannot keep up
modules.productionQuestion: Replica CPU is low but lag grows during a write burst. Which resource is the bottleneck?
modules.learningDelta: Replication apply is often single-threaded or limited by I/O; more replicas do not fix a slow apply path
modules.simMechanic: Primary write burst; replica apply threads and lag
modules.breakCondition: Apply lag grows while replica CPU is idle

modules.title: Connection Storms After Failover
modules.purpose: Prevent every client from reconnecting at once
modules.productionQuestion: A failover triggers 10k reconnects and the new writer is overwhelmed. How do you dampen it?
modules.learningDelta: Reconnect storms need jitter, backoff, connection pooling, and pre-warmed capacity; immediate retries amplify the failover
modules.simMechanic: Failover with reconnect policy; connection spike
modules.breakCondition: The new writer is overwhelmed by synchronized reconnects
modules.sources: AWS RDS Proxy docs; AWS Builders' Library

modules.title: Cold Read Replicas
modules.purpose: Understand why a new replica is slow
modules.productionQuestion: You add a read replica during an incident and it makes latency worse. Why?
modules.learningDelta: A new replica must catch up and warm its cache; reads routed too early hit cold storage and increase lag
modules.simMechanic: Add replica during load; lag, cache hit, latency
modules.breakCondition: A cold replica serves slow reads and falls further behind
modules.sources: AWS RDS replica docs; PostgreSQL docs

modules.title: Aurora Backtrack
modules.purpose: Rewind a cluster without a full restore
modules.productionQuestion: A bad migration changed data 20 minutes ago. Can you rewind instead of restoring?
modules.learningDelta: Aurora Backtrack rewinds cluster state within a retention window, but it is not a substitute for backups and has limits
modules.simMechanic: Timeline with bad change; backtrack vs restore
modules.breakCondition: Backtrack window is shorter than the time since the change

modules.title: Connection Leaks
modules.purpose: Find the code path that never returns a connection
modules.productionQuestion: The pool is exhausted but request rate is normal. Where did the connections go?
modules.learningDelta: A connection leak holds a session after an error path; pool metrics and stack traces reveal it, but only if timeouts and close paths are correct
modules.simMechanic: Service with leaky path; pool usage grows
modules.breakCondition: Pool exhausts and all requests wait
modules.sources: PostgreSQL pool docs; app framework docs

modules.title: MongoDB Replica Sets
modules.purpose: Explain primary, secondaries, and elections
modules.productionQuestion: The primary disappears and the app reconnects to a new node. What happened underneath?
modules.learningDelta: A replica set elects one primary; secondaries apply the oplog, and clients discover topology changes
modules.simMechanic: Replica set with primary failure; election and reconnect
modules.breakCondition: Clients keep using the old primary after election
modules.interviewAngle: Draw a replica set; explain election

modules.title: Read Preference
modules.purpose: Route reads without breaking the product's freshness needs
modules.productionQuestion: A dashboard reads from a lagging secondary and shows old data. Which read preference fits?
modules.learningDelta: Read preference trades freshness for locality and load; primary, primaryPreferred, secondary, and nearest have different failure behavior
modules.simMechanic: Replica set with read preference switch; latency and staleness
modules.breakCondition: A freshness-critical read goes to a lagging secondary

modules.title: Write Concern
modules.purpose: Choose durability and latency deliberately
modules.productionQuestion: A write is acknowledged and then lost after a primary crash. What write concern was used?
modules.learningDelta: Write concern controls how many nodes acknowledge before success; w:1 is fast but can lose writes on failover
modules.simMechanic: Replica set with write concern switch; latency and lost writes
modules.breakCondition: Acknowledged writes are lost after primary failure

modules.title: Adding Readers During an Incident
modules.purpose: Avoid making an incident worse with a new secondary
modules.productionQuestion: The primary is overloaded, so you add a secondary. Why did latency get worse?
modules.learningDelta: A new secondary performs an initial sync and then serves cold reads; it increases primary load and replication pressure before it helps
modules.simMechanic: Primary under load; add a secondary and route reads
modules.breakCondition: Initial sync saturates the primary and lag grows
modules.interviewAngle: Decide whether to add a reader
modules.sources: MongoDB replica set docs; MongoDB production notes

modules.title: Cold Secondaries
modules.purpose: Understand the cache cost of a new replica
modules.productionQuestion: A secondary has low CPU but serves reads slowly. Why?
modules.learningDelta: A new secondary has a cold WiredTiger cache; serving reads before it warms up increases disk I/O and latency
modules.simMechanic: New secondary with cache fill; read latency and disk I/O
modules.breakCondition: Reads routed to a cold secondary exceed the latency SLO

modules.title: Replication Lag and the Oplog
modules.purpose: Detect a secondary that cannot keep up
modules.productionQuestion: Replica lag grows during a write burst and then the secondary falls off the oplog. What happens?
modules.learningDelta: Secondaries apply the capped oplog; if they fall behind the window they need a full resync, not a quick catch-up
modules.simMechanic: Oplog window with write rate; lag and resync
modules.breakCondition: The secondary falls off the oplog and requires resync

modules.title: Elections and Availability
modules.purpose: Explain why writes fail briefly during failover
modules.productionQuestion: The primary failed and writes failed for 12 seconds. What determines that window?
modules.learningDelta: Elections require a majority and take time; electionTimeout, heartbeat, and catch-up determine write availability
modules.simMechanic: Replica set with failure and election timer; write outage
modules.breakCondition: Election takes longer than the write timeout budget

modules.title: Sharding Architecture
modules.purpose: Place mongos, config servers, and shards correctly
modules.productionQuestion: A sharded cluster routes queries slowly. Which component is involved?
modules.learningDelta: mongos routes queries using config server metadata; shards hold data, and routing decisions depend on the shard key
modules.simMechanic: Sharded cluster with query path; routing latency
modules.breakCondition: A scatter-gather query hits every shard

modules.title: Shard Key Design
modules.purpose: Choose a key that distributes writes and supports queries
modules.productionQuestion: One shard key gives perfect distribution but every query is scatter-gather. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: Shard keys must balance write distribution and query locality; high cardinality alone is not enough
modules.simMechanic: Key candidates with query patterns; distribution and query cost
modules.breakCondition: A shard key creates hotspots or scatter-gather queries
modules.interviewAngle: Choose a shard key; explain tradeoff

modules.title: Hot Shards
modules.purpose: Find the shard taking disproportionate writes
modules.productionQuestion: One shard has 80% CPU and the others are idle. Is the balancer broken?
modules.learningDelta: The balancer moves chunks, but a hot key within a chunk or a monotonically increasing key can keep one shard hot
modules.simMechanic: Sharded cluster with key distribution; per-shard CPU
modules.breakCondition: One shard saturates while chunks appear balanced
modules.sources: MongoDB sharding docs; MongoDB balancer docs

modules.title: Chunk Migration
modules.purpose: Move data without hurting latency
modules.productionQuestion: The balancer starts migrating chunks and p99 rises. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Chunk migration copies data and updates metadata; it consumes I/O and network and can compete with application traffic
modules.simMechanic: Sharded cluster with migration; latency and migration rate
modules.breakCondition: Migration consumes I/O and breaches p99

modules.title: The Balancer
modules.purpose: Decide when balancing helps and when it hurts
modules.productionQuestion: Chunks are imbalanced but the balancer is off. Should you turn it on during peak?
modules.learningDelta: The balancer improves distribution over time but adds load; windows and thresholds determine whether it helps during an incident
modules.simMechanic: Cluster with balancer toggle; balance and latency
modules.breakCondition: Balancing during peak makes latency worse

modules.title: Connection Storms
modules.purpose: Protect mongos and shards from reconnect waves
modules.productionQuestion: A network blip causes every app worker to reconnect and mongos CPU spikes. How do you dampen it?
modules.learningDelta: MongoDB drivers pool connections; synchronized reconnects overwhelm mongos and shards without backoff and pool limits
modules.simMechanic: App fleet reconnect with jitter; mongos load
modules.breakCondition: Reconnect storm saturates mongos

modules.title: Index Design
modules.purpose: Build compound indexes that match query shapes
modules.productionQuestion: A compound index is not used even though its fields appear in the query. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Index field order, sort direction, and predicate shape determine whether MongoDB can use an index efficiently
modules.simMechanic: Query shapes with index builder; scanned documents and latency
modules.breakCondition: An index prefix mismatch forces a collection scan

modules.title: Aggregation Pipeline Performance
modules.purpose: Push filters and limits before the expensive stages
modules.productionQuestion: An aggregation pipeline is slow even with an index. Where is the work happening?
modules.learningDelta: Pipeline stage order determines whether indexes, memory, and disk are used; early filters and limits reduce work
modules.simMechanic: Pipeline editor with stage order; docs scanned and latency
modules.breakCondition: A late $match forces a full scan and disk spill

modules.title: Change Streams
modules.purpose: React to writes without polling the collection
modules.productionQuestion: A downstream service polls MongoDB every second and adds load. Can it subscribe instead?
modules.learningDelta: Change streams expose a resumable oplog cursor; resume tokens and majority read concern determine durability and replay
modules.simMechanic: Change stream consumer with interruption; event delivery
modules.breakCondition: A consumer loses its resume token and misses events

modules.title: Retryable Writes
modules.purpose: Make transient failover errors safe to retry
modules.productionQuestion: A write fails during failover and the driver retries it. Could it apply twice?
modules.learningDelta: Retryable writes use a session and transaction number so the server can deduplicate retries within a window
modules.simMechanic: Writes during failover; duplicate effects and retries
modules.breakCondition: A retry is applied twice without retryable semantics

modules.title: Transactions and Their Limits
modules.purpose: Use multi-document transactions when the boundary is real
modules.productionQuestion: A transaction spans 10 minutes and 50k documents. What breaks first?
modules.learningDelta: MongoDB transactions have time and size limits and hold resources; they are not a substitute for schema design
modules.simMechanic: Long transaction with document count; abort and resource use
modules.breakCondition: A transaction exceeds its lifetime and aborts

modules.title: Backup and Restore
modules.purpose: Recover a replica set or sharded cluster coherently
modules.productionQuestion: A restore of one shard completes but the cluster is inconsistent. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Cluster-consistent backups require coordination across shards and config servers; restoring one node is not a cluster restore
modules.simMechanic: Sharded cluster restore; consistency check
modules.breakCondition: Restoring shards independently loses cross-shard consistency

modules.title: Write Amplification
modules.purpose: See why one write costs many I/O operations
modules.productionQuestion: Write throughput drops and disk I/O is saturated. What is write amplification doing?
modules.learningDelta: Indexes, journaling, replication, and document growth multiply physical writes; more indexes can hurt write capacity
modules.simMechanic: Write path with index count; I/O and throughput
modules.breakCondition: Index maintenance saturates disk I/O at peak writes

modules.title: Read Concern
modules.purpose: Choose the consistency of a read
modules.productionQuestion: A read returns data that is later rolled back. Which read concern was used?
modules.learningDelta: Read concern controls the visibility and durability of reads; local can return data not yet majority-committed
modules.simMechanic: Read timeline with concern switch; rolled-back reads
modules.breakCondition: A local read returns a write that is later rolled back

modules.title: Mongos Routing and Targets
modules.purpose: Diagnose a slow query across a sharded cluster
modules.productionQuestion: A query is slow only when it goes through mongos. What do you inspect?
modules.learningDelta: Mongos routes by shard key, merges results, and applies targeting; scatter-gather and merge overhead can dominate
modules.simMechanic: Sharded query path with targeting; shards touched and latency
modules.breakCondition: A query fans out to every shard and merge latency dominates

modules.title: Kafka Partitions: The Unit of Parallelism
modules.purpose: Reason about ordering, throughput, and consumer scaling
modules.productionQuestion: A topic has 12 partitions and 20 consumers. Why are 8 consumers idle?
modules.learningDelta: A partition is consumed by one consumer per group; partition count caps consumer parallelism and sets ordering scope
modules.simMechanic: Topic with partitions and consumers; assignment and lag
modules.breakCondition: Consumers exceed partitions and sit idle

modules.title: Keys and Ordering
modules.purpose: Keep per-entity order without global serialization
modules.productionQuestion: Two updates for one order arrive out of order. What key should the producer use?
modules.learningDelta: Kafka preserves order within a partition; keying by entity keeps its events ordered while allowing parallelism across keys
modules.simMechanic: Producer with key strategy; per-key order and partition load
modules.breakCondition: Related events land on different partitions and reorder

modules.title: Consumer Groups and Offsets
modules.purpose: Understand lag, commits, and replay
modules.productionQuestion: A consumer restarts and reprocesses 10 minutes of events. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Offsets are committed by the group; commit interval and processing semantics determine replay and duplicates
modules.simMechanic: Consumer group with commit policy; duplicates and replay
modules.breakCondition: A crash replays already processed events

modules.title: Rebalancing: Stop the World
modules.purpose: Reduce consumer pauses during scaling and failure
modules.productionQuestion: Adding one consumer pauses the whole group for 40 seconds. What causes the pause?
modules.learningDelta: Rebalances revoke and reassign partitions; eager protocols pause all consumers, cooperative protocols reduce the blast radius
modules.simMechanic: Consumer group scaling; processing pause and lag
modules.breakCondition: A rebalance pauses processing and lag spikes
modules.sources: Kafka consumer rebalance docs; Confluent cooperative sticky

modules.title: Kafka Hot Partition
modules.purpose: Spread one key that dominates a topic
modules.productionQuestion: One partition is at 100% and the others are idle because one key is 60% of traffic. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: Hot partitions come from key skew; salting, key redesign, or splitting the event changes ordering and consumer logic
modules.simMechanic: Topic with key distribution; per-partition throughput and lag
modules.breakCondition: One partition saturates while consumers lag on it only
modules.sources: Confluent hot partition guidance; Kafka docs

modules.title: Partition Count: More Is Not Free
modules.purpose: Choose a partition count for throughput and recovery
modules.productionQuestion: The topic has 200 partitions and failover takes minutes. What did the partition count cost?
modules.learningDelta: More partitions add parallelism but increase metadata, rebalance time, file handles, and end-to-end latency
modules.simMechanic: Topic with partition count; throughput and recovery time
modules.breakCondition: Controller failover slows because of excessive partitions
modules.sources: Kafka docs; Confluent partitioning best practices

modules.title: Retention and Replay
modules.purpose: Keep enough history to recover without unbounded cost
modules.productionQuestion: A consumer is down for two days and retention is 24 hours. What happens?
modules.learningDelta: Retention bounds replay; time and size limits delete segments, and a consumer beyond the window loses data
modules.simMechanic: Topic with retention and consumer outage; available offsets
modules.breakCondition: A consumer falls behind retention and loses events

modules.title: Producer Acks
modules.purpose: Choose durability versus latency
modules.productionQuestion: A producer returns success and the broker loses the event. What acks setting was used?
modules.learningDelta: acks=0/1/all trade latency for durability; acks=all with min.insync.replicas is required for strong guarantees
modules.simMechanic: Producer with acks and ISR; lost events and latency
modules.breakCondition: Acknowledged events are lost on leader failure

modules.title: Idempotent Producer
modules.purpose: Stop retries from duplicating events
modules.productionQuestion: A producer retries a batch and the consumer sees duplicates. What fixes it?
modules.learningDelta: Idempotent producers use sequence numbers and producer IDs to deduplicate retries within a session
modules.simMechanic: Producer retries with idempotence toggle; duplicates
modules.breakCondition: Retries create duplicate records

modules.title: Backpressure in Streaming
modules.purpose: Keep a fast producer from overwhelming consumers
modules.productionQuestion: The producer outruns consumers and lag grows without bound. Where do you apply backpressure?
modules.learningDelta: Backpressure can throttle producers, buffer durably in the log, or shed work; the log is not infinite and lag is a debt
modules.simMechanic: Producer and consumer rates; lag and memory
modules.breakCondition: Lag grows until retention or memory is exhausted

modules.title: Consumer Lag: The Real SLO
modules.purpose: Alert on time-to-catch-up, not just message count
modules.productionQuestion: Consumer lag is 2 million messages. Is that bad?
modules.learningDelta: Lag must be interpreted with production rate and processing rate; time-to-catch-up is the user-facing signal
modules.simMechanic: Topic with lag; messages and time to drain
modules.breakCondition: Lag grows because processing rate is below production

modules.title: Slow Consumers
modules.purpose: Find why one consumer holds back a partition
modules.productionQuestion: One consumer processes 10× slower than its peers. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: Per-partition processing time, downstream calls, and poison records identify slow consumers; more consumers cannot split one partition
modules.simMechanic: Consumer group with per-partition rate; lag by partition
modules.breakCondition: One partition's lag grows without bound

modules.title: Poison Messages
modules.purpose: Stop one bad record from blocking a partition
modules.productionQuestion: One malformed event fails every retry and the partition stops. How do you recover?
modules.learningDelta: A poison message blocks in-order processing; validation, retry limits, and DLQs isolate it without losing the stream
modules.simMechanic: Partition with a failing record; retry and block
modules.breakCondition: A single record halts the partition indefinitely
modules.sources: Kafka error handling docs; Confluent DLQ guidance

modules.title: Dead Letter Queues
modules.purpose: Isolate failures without hiding them
modules.productionQuestion: Failed events go to a DLQ and no one notices for a week. What is missing?
modules.learningDelta: A DLQ is only useful with replay, alerting, ownership, and a retention policy; otherwise it becomes a data dump
modules.simMechanic: Failed event stream; DLQ depth and replay
modules.breakCondition: DLQ grows silently and events are never recovered
modules.sources: AWS SQS DLQ docs; Kafka patterns

modules.title: Exactly-Once Semantics
modules.purpose: Separate broker guarantees from end-to-end effects
modules.productionQuestion: Kafka is configured for exactly-once, but the sink still has duplicates. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Kafka transactions make broker writes atomic; end-to-end exactly-once requires idempotent sinks or transactional outputs
modules.simMechanic: Pipeline with transaction boundary; duplicates at sink
modules.breakCondition: A sink write succeeds twice after a retry

modules.title: Kafka Transactions
modules.purpose: Group writes and offsets atomically
modules.productionQuestion: A consumer writes output and commits its offset separately, causing duplicates. How do transactions help?
modules.learningDelta: Transactions atomically commit produced records and consumed offsets, but add latency and require transactional consumers
modules.simMechanic: Consumer-producer transaction; crash and duplicate output
modules.breakCondition: A crash between output write and offset commit duplicates

modules.title: Confluent Cloud Operations
modules.purpose: Diagnose cluster limits and networking
modules.productionQuestion: A managed Kafka cluster shows elevated latency and the app team cannot see brokers. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: Managed Kafka exposes throughput, partition, and network limits through metrics and quotas; the broker is not yours to tune
modules.simMechanic: Managed cluster with quota and latency; bottleneck
modules.breakCondition: A cluster quota is hit during a peak

modules.title: Schema Registry and Compatibility
modules.purpose: Evolve events without breaking consumers
modules.productionQuestion: A producer adds a required field and old consumers crash. What compatibility mode?
modules.learningDelta: Schema compatibility modes govern evolution; backward, forward, and full compatibility have different deploy orders
modules.simMechanic: Producer and consumers with schema change; compatibility outcome
modules.breakCondition: A schema change breaks consumers during rollout

modules.title: ksqlDB Queries and State
modules.purpose: Understand state stores and reprocessing
modules.productionQuestion: A ksqlDB query restarts and takes 20 minutes to catch up. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Stateful queries rebuild state stores from the changelog; restart time depends on state size and changelog throughput
modules.simMechanic: Query with state size and restart; catch-up time
modules.breakCondition: State rebuild exceeds the recovery SLO

modules.title: WarpStream on Object Storage
modules.purpose: Reason about Kafka-compatible streaming on S3
modules.productionQuestion: A Kafka-compatible service stores data in object storage. What changes for latency and cost?
modules.learningDelta: Object-storage streaming trades broker-local disk for S3 latency and cost; tail latency and metadata operations dominate
modules.simMechanic: Streaming cluster with storage backend switch; latency and cost
modules.breakCondition: Object-storage latency breaches the consumer SLO

modules.title: Object-Storage Streaming Latency
modules.purpose: Separate throughput from tail latency
modules.productionQuestion: Object storage delivers high throughput but p99 reads are slow. Which workload is affected?
modules.learningDelta: Object storage favors throughput and durability; per-request latency and metadata operations make it unsuitable for some low-latency paths
modules.simMechanic: Read workload with object storage; p99 and throughput
modules.breakCondition: p99 read latency breaches a synchronous request path

modules.title: MQTT QoS 0, 1, and 2
modules.purpose: Choose delivery semantics for constrained devices
modules.productionQuestion: A sensor publishes telemetry and the broker restarts. Which QoS prevents loss?
modules.learningDelta: QoS 0 is fire-and-forget, QoS 1 is at-least-once, QoS 2 is exactly-once at the protocol level with higher overhead
modules.simMechanic: Publisher and subscriber with QoS; lost and duplicate messages
modules.breakCondition: QoS 0 loses messages during a broker restart

modules.title: MQTT Retained Messages
modules.purpose: Give new subscribers the current state
modules.productionQuestion: A dashboard reconnects and shows no values until the next publish. What do you enable?
modules.learningDelta: Retained messages store the last value per topic and deliver it on subscribe, trading broker state for freshness
modules.simMechanic: Broker with retained toggle; new subscriber state
modules.breakCondition: A new subscriber has no state until the next event

modules.title: MQTT Fan-Out
modules.purpose: Scale many subscribers per topic
modules.productionQuestion: One telemetry topic has 50k subscribers and the broker is overloaded. How do you fan out?
modules.learningDelta: MQTT fan-out is broker-bound; shared subscriptions, topic trees, and bridging distribute subscribers across brokers
modules.simMechanic: Broker with subscriber count; CPU and delivery latency
modules.breakCondition: Broker CPU saturates as subscribers grow

modules.title: MQTT Broker Scaling
modules.purpose: Add brokers without losing session state
modules.productionQuestion: You add a broker and existing clients lose their sessions. Why?
modules.learningDelta: MQTT sessions and retained state are broker-local unless clustered or bridged; scaling requires state strategy
modules.simMechanic: Broker cluster with session state; reconnect and lost state
modules.breakCondition: Sessions are lost when clients reconnect to a new broker

modules.title: SQS Visibility Timeout
modules.purpose: Prevent duplicate processing and stuck messages
modules.productionQuestion: A consumer takes longer than the visibility timeout and the message is processed twice. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Visibility timeout hides a message while it is processed; it must exceed processing time or be extended, and failures need a DLQ
modules.simMechanic: Queue with consumers; visibility and duplicates
modules.breakCondition: A slow consumer allows a duplicate delivery

modules.title: SQS FIFO
modules.purpose: Get ordering without a single consumer
modules.productionQuestion: You need per-customer order and high throughput. How does FIFO scale?
modules.learningDelta: FIFO queues preserve order within a message group; throughput scales with groups, and a hot group serializes
modules.simMechanic: FIFO queue with groups; ordering and throughput
modules.breakCondition: A hot message group becomes the throughput bottleneck

modules.title: SNS and EventBridge Routing
modules.purpose: Fan out notifications and route events without hidden coupling
modules.productionQuestion: A notification goes to five subscribers and a new event triggers three unintended consumers. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: SNS fan-out and EventBridge rules solve different routing problems; broad patterns and shared buses create hidden consumers and ordering surprises
modules.simMechanic: Topics, subscriptions, and rules; matched consumers and fan-out
modules.breakCondition: A broad rule or subscription routes an event to the wrong consumers
modules.sources: AWS SNS docs; AWS EventBridge docs

modules.title: Transactional Outbox
modules.purpose: Publish events without dual-write failures
modules.productionQuestion: The database commit succeeds and the Kafka publish fails. How do you keep them consistent?
modules.learningDelta: The outbox pattern writes the event in the same transaction and publishes it asynchronously, using polling or CDC
modules.simMechanic: Database plus outbox and publisher; crash between steps
modules.breakCondition: A dual write loses the event or publishes without commit

modules.title: Change Data Capture
modules.purpose: Stream database changes without polling
modules.productionQuestion: A downstream index lags by an hour because it polls the database. Can CDC help?
modules.learningDelta: CDC reads the database log and emits ordered changes; snapshotting, schema changes, and tombstones add complexity
modules.simMechanic: Database log to stream; lag and event ordering
modules.breakCondition: A schema change breaks the CDC pipeline

modules.title: Queue Depth vs Latency
modules.purpose: Use the right backlog signal
modules.productionQuestion: Queue depth is 10k but latency is fine; another queue has depth 100 and is timing out. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Queue depth alone is ambiguous; arrival rate, service rate, and age of oldest message determine user impact
modules.simMechanic: Two queues with different rates; depth and wait time
modules.breakCondition: A shallow queue has high wait because service is slow
modules.sources: AWS SQS metrics docs; Google SRE Book

modules.title: Kafka ISR and Under-Replicated Partitions
modules.purpose: Detect durability risk before a broker loss
modules.productionQuestion: One broker is down and partitions are under-replicated. Are writes still safe?
modules.learningDelta: ISR tracks in-sync replicas; min.insync.replicas and acks determine whether writes continue and whether durability is reduced
modules.simMechanic: Cluster with broker failure; ISR and write acceptance
modules.breakCondition: Writes fail or lose durability when ISR falls below the minimum

modules.title: ECS Task Definitions
modules.purpose: Understand the immutable unit of deployment
modules.productionQuestion: A task restarts with different environment variables than the last run. Where do you look?
modules.learningDelta: A task definition is an immutable revision of image, CPU, memory, env, volumes, and IAM; services pin a revision
modules.simMechanic: Task definition inspector; revision change and task launch
modules.breakCondition: A service launches an old or mismatched revision

modules.title: ECS Services and Desired Count
modules.purpose: Reconcile desired state with reality
modules.productionQuestion: The service says 10 tasks desired but only 6 are running. What does ECS do next?
modules.learningDelta: A service continuously reconciles desired count with running tasks through the scheduler and deployment configuration
modules.simMechanic: Service with desired and running tasks; reconciliation
modules.breakCondition: Desired count cannot be reached because of capacity or health

modules.title: ECS Placement
modules.purpose: Spread tasks without breaking capacity
modules.productionQuestion: All tasks land on one container instance and it saturates. How do you spread them?
modules.learningDelta: Placement strategies and constraints control bin packing and spread; Fargate abstracts instances but not AZ spread
modules.simMechanic: Cluster with placement strategy; per-instance utilization
modules.breakCondition: Ten tasks land on one instance and saturate it

modules.title: Target Tracking Scaling
modules.purpose: Scale on the signal that actually predicts load
modules.productionQuestion: CPU stays at 40% while latency rises and the service does not scale. What metric should drive scaling?
modules.learningDelta: Target tracking follows a metric and a target; choosing CPU when the bottleneck is queue depth or concurrency causes late scaling
modules.simMechanic: Service with scaling policy; load, metric, and task count
modules.breakCondition: The scaling metric stays low while latency breaches SLO

modules.title: Step Scaling
modules.purpose: React to thresholds without oscillating
modules.productionQuestion: Traffic crosses a threshold repeatedly and the service flaps between 4 and 20 tasks. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Step scaling uses thresholds and cooldowns; missing scale-in stabilization causes oscillation and cold starts
modules.simMechanic: Service with step policy; traffic wave and task count
modules.breakCondition: Scale-in/out oscillation exhausts capacity and latency

modules.title: Scaling Cooldowns and Stabilization
modules.purpose: Avoid scaling on noise
modules.productionQuestion: A one-minute spike triggers 30 tasks and then they all scale in. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Cooldowns and stabilization windows filter noise but delay response; the right values depend on workload duration
modules.simMechanic: Bursty traffic with cooldown sliders; task churn and latency
modules.breakCondition: Scaling reacts to a transient spike and then over-corrects

modules.title: ECS Deployment Circuit Breaker
modules.purpose: Roll back a bad deployment automatically
modules.productionQuestion: A new task revision fails health checks and the deployment hangs. How do you make ECS roll back?
modules.learningDelta: The deployment circuit breaker detects repeated task failures and can roll back automatically when configured
modules.simMechanic: Deployment with failing revision; automatic rollback
modules.breakCondition: A bad revision loops without rollback and old capacity is lost
modules.sources: AWS ECS deployment circuit breaker docs

modules.title: ECS Rolling Deployments
modules.purpose: Keep capacity during rollout
modules.productionQuestion: A rolling deployment drops below the minimum healthy percent and causes 503s. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: minimumHealthyPercent and maximumPercent control rolling capacity; task draining and health checks determine actual availability
modules.simMechanic: Service rollout; capacity during deployment
modules.breakCondition: Capacity falls below the minimum and requests fail

modules.title: Fargate Cold Starts
modules.purpose: Account for time before a task serves traffic
modules.productionQuestion: Autoscaling adds tasks but p99 still spikes for two minutes. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Fargate tasks need scheduling, image pull, startup, and health check time before serving; scaling must anticipate it
modules.simMechanic: Scale-out with task startup phases; time to serve
modules.breakCondition: New tasks are too slow to absorb the spike
modules.sources: AWS Fargate docs; AWS containers blog

modules.title: Image Pull and Registry Limits
modules.purpose: Stop deployments from stalling on image pulls
modules.productionQuestion: New tasks take 90 seconds to start and the registry is throttling. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Image size, layers, cache, and registry pull limits determine task startup; a large image multiplies cold-start cost
modules.simMechanic: Task startup with image size and pull rate; time to ready
modules.breakCondition: Registry throttles pulls and tasks stay pending
modules.sources: AWS ECR docs; Docker image best practices

modules.title: ALB Target Registration for ECS
modules.purpose: Get tasks into the target group reliably
modules.productionQuestion: A task is running but receives no traffic. What registration state do you check?
modules.learningDelta: ECS registers tasks by IP or instance; target group health, security groups, and ports decide traffic
modules.simMechanic: Service registration to ALB; healthy targets
modules.breakCondition: A running task never becomes a healthy target

modules.title: Task Draining
modules.purpose: Remove tasks without cutting requests
modules.productionQuestion: A deployment causes 502s during task stop. What is the drain sequence?
modules.learningDelta: ECS deregisters a task, waits for draining, then stops it; timeout and connection behavior decide in-flight request loss
modules.simMechanic: Task replacement with drain timer; failed requests
modules.breakCondition: In-flight requests are cut when the task stops

modules.title: ECS Exec
modules.purpose: Debug a live task without SSH
modules.productionQuestion: A task is unhealthy but you cannot shell in. How do you inspect it?
modules.learningDelta: ECS Exec uses SSM to run commands in a running task; it requires task role, SSM agent, and audit controls
modules.simMechanic: Task shell with Exec enabled; inspect process and files
modules.breakCondition: Exec is unavailable because of IAM or agent configuration

modules.title: ECS Logs
modules.purpose: Find logs after a task disappears
modules.productionQuestion: A task was OOM-killed and its container is gone. Where are the logs?
modules.learningDelta: ECS log drivers ship stdout/stderr to CloudWatch or FireLens; task stop reason and previous logs are separate signals
modules.simMechanic: Task lifecycle with logs; stop reason
modules.breakCondition: Logs are missing because the driver or stream is misconfigured

modules.title: Container Health Checks
modules.purpose: Distinguish liveness from readiness
modules.productionQuestion: A task is healthy but not ready, or ready but dead. Which check do you fix?
modules.learningDelta: Container and load balancer health checks answer different questions; liveness restarts, readiness removes traffic
modules.simMechanic: Task with both checks; restart and traffic removal
modules.breakCondition: A liveness check restarts a task that is merely warming up

modules.title: Service Discovery
modules.purpose: Resolve services without hard-coded IPs
modules.productionQuestion: A service calls another by IP and a task replacement breaks it. What do you use?
modules.learningDelta: Service discovery maps stable names to changing task IPs; DNS TTL and health determine failover
modules.simMechanic: Service registry with task churn; DNS resolution
modules.breakCondition: A stale DNS record routes to a dead task

modules.title: Cloud Map
modules.purpose: Register and discover ECS services
modules.productionQuestion: You need private DNS for 40 services. How does Cloud Map work?
modules.learningDelta: Cloud Map maintains namespaces and service instances; health checks and TTLs control resolution and failover
modules.simMechanic: Service registry with instances; query results
modules.breakCondition: Unhealthy instances stay registered and receive traffic

modules.title: CPU and Memory Limits
modules.purpose: Prevent one task from starving its neighbors
modules.productionQuestion: One task uses all node memory and other tasks are evicted. How do limits work?
modules.learningDelta: Container and task limits bound CPU and memory; reservations influence placement, and exceeding memory leads to OOM
modules.simMechanic: Node with tasks; limits and eviction
modules.breakCondition: A task exceeds memory and is killed or starves peers

modules.title: OOM Kills
modules.purpose: Find what consumed memory before the kill
modules.productionQuestion: A task restarts with exit code 137. Was it CPU throttling or memory?
modules.learningDelta: Exit 137 is SIGKILL; OOM kills leave a stop reason and memory metrics, while CPU throttling does not kill
modules.simMechanic: Task memory usage; OOM at the limit
modules.breakCondition: Memory exceeds the limit and the task is killed
modules.sources: AWS ECS OOM docs; Linux cgroups docs

modules.title: Task IAM Roles
modules.purpose: Give tasks least privilege without static keys
modules.productionQuestion: A task needs S3 access but the node role can read everything. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Task roles are per-task credentials delivered by the agent; execution roles are separate and used to pull images and write logs
modules.simMechanic: Task with role switch; allowed and denied calls
modules.breakCondition: A task has more permissions than its workload needs

modules.title: Secrets in ECS
modules.purpose: Inject secrets without baking them into images
modules.productionQuestion: A database password is in an environment variable in the task definition. What is the safer path?
modules.learningDelta: Secrets Manager or SSM parameters can be injected at task start; image, task definition, and logs must stay free of secrets
modules.simMechanic: Task with secret sources; leaked secret and rotation
modules.breakCondition: A secret appears in the task definition or logs

modules.title: Capacity Providers
modules.purpose: Mix Fargate and EC2 without surprises
modules.productionQuestion: A service moves to a capacity provider and tasks fail to place. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Capacity providers define capacity and strategy; weights, base, and instance types determine placement and cost
modules.simMechanic: Cluster with providers; placement and cost
modules.breakCondition: Tasks cannot place because the provider lacks capacity

modules.title: Multi-AZ Scheduling
modules.purpose: Spread tasks across zones
modules.productionQuestion: One AZ loses a node and too many tasks were packed there. How do you spread them?
modules.learningDelta: The scheduler places tasks across zones, but capacity and placement constraints can concentrate them
modules.simMechanic: Cluster across AZs; AZ failure and remaining capacity
modules.breakCondition: One AZ failure removes more capacity than N+1 covers

modules.title: Batch vs Service
modules.purpose: Choose the right ECS scheduler
modules.productionQuestion: A nightly job runs as a service and restarts forever. What should it be?
modules.learningDelta: Services maintain desired count; batch jobs run to completion and retry differently, with different observability
modules.simMechanic: Workload switch between service and batch; completion and cost
modules.breakCondition: A finite job is restarted indefinitely as a service

modules.title: Sidecar Patterns
modules.purpose: Add logging, proxy, or security without breaking tasks
modules.productionQuestion: A sidecar doubles task CPU and the service is throttled. What do you check?
modules.learningDelta: Sidecars share task resources; CPU/memory limits and startup order affect the main container
modules.simMechanic: Task with sidecars; resource contention
modules.breakCondition: Sidecar consumes the task's CPU and main container throttles
modules.sources: AWS ECS sidecar docs; Envoy sidecar docs

modules.title: Fargate Spot
modules.purpose: Use interruption-tolerant capacity
modules.productionQuestion: Fargate Spot is cheaper but tasks disappear. Which workloads fit?
modules.learningDelta: Fargate Spot uses spare capacity with interruption notices; stateless, retryable, and drained workloads tolerate it
modules.simMechanic: Service on Spot with interruption; task churn and cost
modules.breakCondition: An interruption removes tasks without enough healthy capacity

modules.title: Envoy Listeners
modules.purpose: Understand where traffic enters the proxy
modules.productionQuestion: A request never reaches the service. Which Envoy listener should have accepted it?
modules.learningDelta: Envoy listeners bind addresses and ports and pass connections into filter chains and route configuration
modules.simMechanic: Proxy config with listener mismatch; request outcome
modules.breakCondition: Traffic arrives on a port no listener serves

modules.title: Envoy Clusters and Endpoints
modules.purpose: See how the proxy chooses a backend
modules.productionQuestion: The mesh reports no healthy upstreams while pods are running. Which cluster view do you check?
modules.learningDelta: Envoy clusters group endpoints and health; outlier ejection and endpoint discovery determine usable capacity
modules.simMechanic: Proxy with endpoints; healthy and ejected hosts
modules.breakCondition: All endpoints are ejected or missing from the cluster

modules.title: Envoy Routes
modules.purpose: Route by host, path, and header without surprises
modules.productionQuestion: A canary route works for one header but all traffic hits the stable version. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Routes match in order; host/path/header predicates and route order decide which cluster receives traffic
modules.simMechanic: Route table with precedence; traffic split
modules.breakCondition: A broad route shadows the intended canary route

modules.title: Kuma Control Plane
modules.purpose: Separate data plane behavior from control plane policy
modules.productionQuestion: A policy applies to half the mesh and no one knows why. Where is the selector?
modules.learningDelta: Kuma's control plane distributes policies to selected data plane proxies; selectors, mesh scope, and versions decide where they apply
modules.simMechanic: Kuma policy with selectors; affected services
modules.breakCondition: A policy selector misses or overmatches workloads

modules.title: mTLS in the Mesh
modules.purpose: Encrypt and authenticate service traffic
modules.productionQuestion: A service accepts plaintext from inside the mesh. What policy prevents it?
modules.learningDelta: mTLS authenticates both sides with certificates; permissive mode allows plaintext and hides misconfiguration
modules.simMechanic: Mesh with mTLS modes; allowed and rejected traffic
modules.breakCondition: A workload talks plaintext because permissive mode is on

modules.title: Mesh Retries
modules.purpose: Retry safely at the proxy layer
modules.productionQuestion: Envoy retries every 503 three times and the dependency collapses. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: Proxy retries are powerful and dangerous; retry budgets, conditions, and per-try timeout prevent amplification
modules.simMechanic: Proxy with retry policy; upstream RPS and success
modules.breakCondition: Retries multiply load and prevent recovery

modules.title: Mesh Timeouts
modules.purpose: Set deadlines at the right layer
modules.productionQuestion: The proxy returns 504 before the service finishes. Which timeout won?
modules.learningDelta: Proxy timeout, route timeout, and application deadline are separate; the smallest wins and retries can stack
modules.simMechanic: Chain with proxy and app timeouts; which fires
modules.breakCondition: Proxy timeout cuts a request the app would have completed

modules.title: Mesh Circuit Breaking
modules.purpose: Shed load before the dependency fails
modules.productionQuestion: A dependency is slow and Envoy keeps opening new connections. What limits do you set?
modules.learningDelta: Envoy circuit breakers cap connections, pending requests, and retries; they protect the upstream and fail fast locally
modules.simMechanic: Proxy with breaker limits; upstream load and local failures
modules.breakCondition: Pending requests grow without bound and latency explodes

modules.title: Outlier Detection
modules.purpose: Eject bad endpoints without ejecting the fleet
modules.productionQuestion: One pod returns errors and Envoy ejects healthy pods too. What threshold is wrong?
modules.learningDelta: Outlier detection ejects hosts based on consecutive errors and ejection percentage; overly aggressive settings remove capacity
modules.simMechanic: Endpoint pool with failures; ejected hosts and capacity
modules.breakCondition: Ejection removes too much capacity and causes an outage

modules.title: Traffic Splitting
modules.purpose: Shift traffic without changing clients
modules.productionQuestion: You need 5% canary traffic and instant rollback. Where do you implement it?
modules.learningDelta: Mesh traffic splitting weights clusters by route; it is fast to change but must align with observability and health
modules.simMechanic: Two versions with weight slider; errors and latency
modules.breakCondition: A weight change sends traffic to an unready version
modules.sources: Kuma traffic routing docs; Envoy weighted clusters

modules.title: Canary Through the Mesh
modules.purpose: Gate a rollout on real signals
modules.productionQuestion: The canary has 5% traffic and no errors; can you increase to 100%?
modules.learningDelta: A canary needs a representative metric gate, enough traffic, and capacity headroom; low traffic hides tail failures
modules.simMechanic: Canary weight with metric gate; error and latency signals
modules.breakCondition: Canary passes on low traffic but fails at full capacity
modules.interviewAngle: Design canary gate; explain sample size
modules.sources: Google SRE Workbook; Kuma canary docs

modules.title: Mesh Access Logs
modules.purpose: Debug request failures at the proxy
modules.productionQuestion: The app has no log for a failed request. Does the mesh?
modules.learningDelta: Access logs record proxy-level status, upstream, timing, and flags; they explain failures before the app sees them
modules.simMechanic: Proxy log stream; failed request trace
modules.breakCondition: The failure is only visible in proxy logs

modules.title: Mesh Tracing
modules.purpose: Connect proxy and application spans
modules.productionQuestion: Traces stop at the sidecar and do not show the upstream call. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Mesh tracing requires context propagation and proxy span generation; sampling and header handling decide continuity
modules.simMechanic: Trace through proxy; missing span
modules.breakCondition: Proxy spans are disconnected from application spans

modules.title: Sidecar Overhead
modules.purpose: Measure the cost of the mesh
modules.productionQuestion: Latency rose after enabling the mesh. How much is the sidecar?
modules.learningDelta: Sidecars add hops, CPU, memory, and connection pools; the cost is visible in per-hop latency and resource usage
modules.simMechanic: Service with and without sidecar; p99 and resource use
modules.breakCondition: Sidecar CPU throttling adds tail latency

modules.title: Ingress Gateway
modules.purpose: Terminate external traffic at the mesh edge
modules.productionQuestion: External traffic bypasses mesh policy and reaches pods directly. What do you change?
modules.learningDelta: An ingress gateway provides a controlled entry point with TLS, routing, and policy; bypass paths defeat mTLS and observability
modules.simMechanic: External client to gateway to service; bypass path
modules.breakCondition: A direct pod path bypasses the gateway and policy
modules.sources: Kuma ingress docs; Envoy gateway docs

modules.title: Cross-Cluster Mesh
modules.purpose: Route across clusters without losing locality
modules.productionQuestion: A failover sends all traffic to one cluster and latency rises. What does the mesh know?
modules.learningDelta: Cross-cluster mesh discovers remote services; locality and failover policy decide whether traffic stays local
modules.simMechanic: Two clusters with failover; traffic distribution
modules.breakCondition: Failover overloads the remote cluster

modules.title: Locality-Aware Load Balancing
modules.purpose: Keep traffic in the zone when it is healthy
modules.productionQuestion: Cross-zone traffic costs rise after a mesh rollout. What policy changed?
modules.learningDelta: Locality-aware balancing prefers local endpoints but fails over when local capacity or health is insufficient
modules.simMechanic: Multi-zone services; local vs cross-zone traffic
modules.breakCondition: Local capacity is insufficient and failover is not configured

modules.title: Mesh Failover
modules.purpose: Move traffic when a zone or cluster fails
modules.productionQuestion: A zone fails and Envoy keeps sending traffic to ejected endpoints. Why?
modules.learningDelta: Failover policy, priority groups, and health checks determine whether traffic moves; stale endpoints cause errors
modules.simMechanic: Zone failure with priorities; traffic and errors
modules.breakCondition: Traffic does not move because priority groups are misconfigured

modules.title: Envoy Retry Storm
modules.purpose: Stop retries from amplifying a dependency failure
modules.productionQuestion: A dependency fails for 5 seconds and request volume triples for 5 minutes. What caused it?
modules.learningDelta: Coordinated proxy retries amplify failure; retry budgets, jitter, and circuit breaking bound the amplification
modules.simMechanic: Proxy mesh with failure; upstream load and recovery
modules.breakCondition: Retry volume prevents the dependency from recovering
modules.sources: Envoy retry docs; Google SRE Book

modules.title: Policy Conflicts
modules.purpose: Predict which mesh policy wins
modules.productionQuestion: Two policies set different timeouts for the same service. Which one applies?
modules.learningDelta: Mesh policy precedence depends on scope and specificity; conflicting policies are hard to debug without a clear ownership model
modules.simMechanic: Policy set with scope; effective config
modules.breakCondition: A broad policy overrides the intended service policy

modules.title: Envoy Admin and Stats
modules.purpose: Inspect the proxy without guessing
modules.productionQuestion: A request fails and the app has no error. What does Envoy admin show?
modules.learningDelta: Envoy admin exposes config dump, clusters, stats, and readiness; it is the fastest way to see proxy-level state
modules.simMechanic: Proxy admin panel; find failing cluster
modules.breakCondition: The issue is invisible in app logs but present in Envoy stats

modules.title: Certificate Rotation
modules.purpose: Rotate mTLS identities without an outage
modules.productionQuestion: Certificates expire at midnight and the mesh starts failing handshakes. What rotation plan?
modules.learningDelta: Certificate rotation needs overlapping validity, trust bundles, and automated reload; short-lived certs reduce risk but require reliable automation
modules.simMechanic: Cert lifecycle with rotation; handshake failures
modules.breakCondition: An expired certificate breaks service-to-service calls

modules.title: Rolling Deployments
modules.purpose: Replace capacity without dropping below the minimum
modules.productionQuestion: A rolling deploy causes a brief 503 spike. What is the capacity math?
modules.learningDelta: Rolling deploys trade capacity for speed; minimum healthy and maximum surge determine whether the fleet survives the transition
modules.simMechanic: Fleet rollout with surge and healthy sliders; available capacity
modules.breakCondition: Available capacity falls below the request rate during rollout
modules.sources: AWS CodeDeploy docs; Kubernetes deployment docs

modules.title: Blue-Green Deployments
modules.purpose: Cut over with a fast rollback path
modules.productionQuestion: A blue-green deploy is ready but the database migration is not reversible. Do you cut over?
modules.learningDelta: Blue-green gives fast traffic cutover and rollback, but shared state and schema changes can make the old environment unusable
modules.simMechanic: Two environments and a switch; traffic and database compatibility
modules.breakCondition: Rollback fails because the schema changed under the old version
modules.sources: AWS blue-green guidance; Google SRE Workbook

modules.title: Canary Deployments
modules.purpose: Limit the blast radius of a bad release
modules.productionQuestion: A release has a bug that affects 1% of requests. How does a canary help?
modules.learningDelta: A canary exposes a small traffic slice to the new version and gates promotion on observed signals
modules.simMechanic: Canary weight and errors; promote or roll back
modules.breakCondition: Canary errors are diluted by stable traffic and the gate passes

modules.title: Feature Flags
modules.purpose: Decouple deploy from release
modules.productionQuestion: The code is deployed but the feature must stay off for one tenant. What do you use?
modules.learningDelta: Flags separate deploy from release; flag scope, defaults, and cleanup determine safety and long-term risk
modules.simMechanic: Flag console with tenant targeting; feature exposure
modules.breakCondition: A flag default enables the feature for everyone

modules.title: Canary with a Metric Gate
modules.purpose: Promote only when the canary proves itself
modules.productionQuestion: The canary passes error rate but fails at full rollout because of capacity. What gate was missing?
modules.learningDelta: A canary gate must cover error rate, latency, saturation, and capacity at the target scale, with enough traffic for confidence
modules.simMechanic: Canary to full rollout with gate metrics; capacity at 100%
modules.breakCondition: Canary passes but full rollout exceeds capacity
modules.sources: Google SRE Workbook; AWS deployment safety

modules.title: Automated Rollback
modules.purpose: Roll back before a human wakes up
modules.productionQuestion: A release raises 5xx at 3 a.m. How fast can rollback happen without a human?
modules.learningDelta: Automated rollback uses health and metric gates plus a tested rollback path; the recovery time is bounded by detection and artifact availability
modules.simMechanic: Release with auto-rollback; detection and recovery time
modules.breakCondition: Rollback is slow because the previous artifact is unavailable
modules.sources: AWS CodeDeploy docs; Google SRE Workbook

modules.title: Blue-Green Database Migrations
modules.purpose: Change schema without breaking either version
modules.productionQuestion: Both blue and green must run during cutover. How do you migrate the database?
modules.learningDelta: Blue-green schema changes require expand/contract compatibility so both versions can read and write during the transition
modules.simMechanic: Two app versions and schema; compatibility outcomes
modules.breakCondition: The old version breaks on the new schema during rollback

modules.title: Expand/Contract Migrations
modules.purpose: Ship schema changes in safe steps
modules.productionQuestion: A column rename breaks the previous release. How do you sequence it?
modules.learningDelta: Expand/contract adds the new shape, backfills, dual-writes, then removes the old shape; each step is independently deployable
modules.simMechanic: Schema timeline with releases; reads and writes
modules.breakCondition: A destructive migration runs before old code is drained
modules.sources: Martin Fowler expand/contract; AWS database migration docs

modules.title: Deployment Verification
modules.purpose: Prove the release works before shifting traffic
modules.productionQuestion: The deploy is green but the checkout path is broken. What verification was missing?
modules.learningDelta: Verification must exercise critical user paths, dependencies, and data, not just process health
modules.simMechanic: Deploy with verification checks; pass/fail and traffic
modules.breakCondition: A broken critical path passes health checks
modules.sources: Google SRE Workbook; AWS deployment docs

modules.title: Smoke Tests
modules.purpose: Catch the obvious before users do
modules.productionQuestion: A new task starts and serves 200 on `/health` but 500 on checkout. What smoke test?
modules.learningDelta: Smoke tests exercise real dependencies and critical writes; health checks alone prove only process liveness
modules.simMechanic: Smoke suite with dependency failures; caught defects
modules.breakCondition: Health checks pass while a critical path is broken

modules.title: Rollback vs Roll-Forward
modules.purpose: Choose the faster safe path under pressure
modules.productionQuestion: A bad release is live and the database has new rows. Do you roll back or fix forward?
modules.learningDelta: Rollback restores known code but may be incompatible with new data; roll-forward is faster only when the fix is understood and tested
modules.simMechanic: Incident with two paths; outcomes and time
modules.breakCondition: Rollback corrupts data written by the new version

modules.title: Traffic Shifting
modules.purpose: Move traffic in controlled increments
modules.productionQuestion: You need 1%, 5%, 25%, 100% with a gate at each step. How do you sequence it?
modules.learningDelta: Traffic shifting is a sequence of exposure steps with gates; step size trades detection time for blast radius
modules.simMechanic: Weighted rollout with steps; errors and exposure
modules.breakCondition: A large step exposes too many users to a bad release
modules.sources: Google SRE Workbook; AWS deployment docs

modules.title: Change Freezes
modules.purpose: Use freezes without creating a bigger risk
modules.productionQuestion: A freeze is active and a critical fix is needed. What is the exception path?
modules.learningDelta: Freezes reduce change risk but concentrate it; exceptions need review, rollback plans, and a clear owner
modules.simMechanic: Calendar with freeze and emergency change; risk
modules.breakCondition: A freeze blocks a necessary fix or lets a risky change through
modules.sources: Google SRE Workbook; ITIL change guidance

modules.title: Change Management That Helps
modules.purpose: Make change review faster and safer
modules.productionQuestion: Every change needs five approvals and incidents still happen. What should change review focus on?
modules.learningDelta: Good change management reviews blast radius, reversibility, observability, and ownership; approval count is not risk control
modules.simMechanic: Change queue with risk scoring; approvals and incidents
modules.breakCondition: A high-risk change is approved without a rollback plan

modules.title: GitOps
modules.purpose: Keep desired state reviewable and reversible
modules.productionQuestion: A manual console change disappears on the next sync. Why?
modules.learningDelta: GitOps makes Git the desired state; drift reconciliation overwrites manual changes, which is safety and a trap
modules.simMechanic: Cluster with GitOps sync; drift and revert
modules.breakCondition: A manual hotfix is reverted by reconciliation during an incident

modules.title: CI/CD Pipeline Design
modules.purpose: Make the pipeline fast enough to be used
modules.productionQuestion: The pipeline takes 90 minutes and teams bypass it. What do you optimize?
modules.learningDelta: Pipeline speed and reliability determine adoption; parallelism, caching, and staged gates reduce lead time without skipping safety
modules.simMechanic: Pipeline stages with duration; lead time and failures
modules.breakCondition: Teams bypass the pipeline because feedback is too slow

modules.title: Immutable Artifacts
modules.purpose: Build once and promote the same bits
modules.productionQuestion: Staging passed but production runs a different build. What went wrong?
modules.learningDelta: Immutable artifacts are built once, identified by digest, and promoted; rebuilding per environment changes the software
modules.simMechanic: Artifact flow across environments; drift
modules.breakCondition: Production runs a different artifact than staging

modules.title: Build Once, Deploy Many
modules.purpose: Keep environments identical
modules.productionQuestion: A config change requires a rebuild and staging diverges. How do you deploy the same artifact with different config?
modules.learningDelta: Configuration belongs outside the artifact; environment-specific config is injected at deploy time, with validation
modules.simMechanic: Artifact and config matrix; environment drift
modules.breakCondition: A config difference causes a production-only failure

modules.title: Config Drift
modules.purpose: Detect the setting that only production has
modules.productionQuestion: Staging and production behave differently after months of manual changes. How do you find drift?
modules.learningDelta: Drift is inevitable without reconciliation and comparison; config as code plus periodic diff reduces surprise
modules.simMechanic: Two environments with drift; diff and incident
modules.breakCondition: A production-only setting causes an outage

modules.title: Shadow Traffic
modules.purpose: Test a new version without user impact
modules.productionQuestion: You need production traffic to validate a rewrite but cannot affect users. What do you do?
modules.learningDelta: Shadow traffic mirrors requests to the new version and discards responses; it validates behavior but doubles load and risks side effects
modules.simMechanic: Mirrored traffic to old and new; load and side effects
modules.breakCondition: Shadow writes duplicate side effects
modules.sources: Envoy request mirroring docs; Google SRE Workbook

modules.title: Dark Launches
modules.purpose: Release code before exposing the feature
modules.productionQuestion: The feature must be deployed for weeks before launch. How do you keep it dark?
modules.learningDelta: Dark launches deploy inactive code paths behind flags and verify them with synthetic or internal traffic
modules.simMechanic: Feature with dark launch; internal checks and exposure
modules.breakCondition: A dark path is exercised by real users before launch

modules.title: Deploying During an Incident
modules.purpose: Decide whether a change helps or hurts
modules.productionQuestion: An incident is active and a fix is ready. Do you deploy now?
modules.learningDelta: Deploys during incidents add variables; prefer reversible config or flags, and deploy only with a clear hypothesis and rollback
modules.simMechanic: Incident with deploy option; outcome and variables
modules.breakCondition: A deploy during the incident obscures the original cause

modules.title: Canary Capacity Fallacy
modules.purpose: Test at the scale that will break
modules.productionQuestion: A canary passes at 5% traffic and the service fails at 100%. Why?
modules.learningDelta: A canary at low traffic does not exercise capacity, caches, locks, or downstream limits at full scale
modules.simMechanic: Canary vs full load; capacity and latency
modules.breakCondition: Full rollout saturates a resource the canary never touched

modules.title: Schema Compatibility
modules.purpose: Keep old and new code working together
modules.productionQuestion: Old and new versions run side by side for an hour. What schema rules apply?
modules.learningDelta: Rolling and canary releases require backward and forward compatible schemas; readers must tolerate missing and extra fields
modules.simMechanic: Two versions with schema change; failures
modules.breakCondition: The old version fails on a field the new version requires

modules.title: Artifact Promotion
modules.purpose: Move a tested artifact through gates
modules.productionQuestion: A release is approved in staging; what exactly moves to production?
modules.learningDelta: Promotion moves the same immutable artifact and provenance, with environment config applied separately
modules.simMechanic: Artifact pipeline; promotion and drift
modules.breakCondition: Rebuilding for production loses the tested artifact identity

modules.title: Deployment Frequency
modules.purpose: Increase speed without increasing risk
modules.productionQuestion: The team deploys monthly and every deploy is an incident. What changes first?
modules.learningDelta: Frequent small deploys reduce change size and improve recovery; the constraint is often test and rollback capability, not deploy tooling
modules.simMechanic: Deploy cadence with change size; incident rate
modules.breakCondition: Large infrequent deploys create higher-risk changes

modules.title: Lead Time for Changes
modules.purpose: Find the queue, not the coding time
modules.productionQuestion: A one-line fix takes two weeks to reach production. Where is the time spent?
modules.learningDelta: Lead time is dominated by queues, approvals, and test duration; optimize the constraint, not the average
modules.simMechanic: Pipeline timeline; stage wait times
modules.breakCondition: Approval queue dominates lead time

modules.title: Rollback Data Loss
modules.purpose: Know what rollback cannot undo
modules.productionQuestion: A rollback restores the old code but the new code sent emails. What is irreversible?
modules.learningDelta: Rollback restores software, not external side effects; migrations, messages, and third-party calls need compensating actions
modules.simMechanic: Incident with rollback; data and side effects
modules.breakCondition: A rollback loses data or repeats an external effect

modules.title: Incident Command
modules.purpose: Run an incident instead of debugging in parallel
modules.productionQuestion: Five engineers are debugging and no one is communicating. What role is missing?
modules.learningDelta: Incident command assigns one coordinator, one communications owner, and one operations owner so investigation and communication do not compete
modules.simMechanic: Incident with role assignment; resolution time and updates
modules.breakCondition: Parallel debugging creates conflicting changes and no updates
modules.sources: PagerDuty incident response docs; Google SRE Book

modules.title: Incident Roles
modules.purpose: Make ownership explicit under pressure
modules.productionQuestion: The database expert is also writing customer updates and misses the fix. How do you staff the incident?
modules.learningDelta: Separate command, operations, communications, and subject-matter roles; one person may hold two only in small incidents
modules.simMechanic: Incident roster with role switching; missed actions
modules.breakCondition: A critical task has no owner and is dropped

modules.title: Communication Cadence
